mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified/notarized copy of passport for each director, shareholder, and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Canada has been a Party to the Apostille Convention since 11 Jan 2024) or Consular Legalization at Canadian embassy/consulate for non-member states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Certificate of Good Standing for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry / competent government authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the United Nations Consolidated List, Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists (under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act), OFAC SDN list, and domestic PEP databases. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, including source-of-funds verification and senior-management approval. Screening is refreshed at onboarding, on name/ownership changes, and at least annually.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry / Service Alberta (CORES and NUANS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be entered in the Latin alphabet. The legal designation 'ULC', 'U.L.C.', or 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' is mandatory for an Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation. Scripts other than Latin require a transliterated English name. Numerals and standard punctuation may be used; obscene or misleading terms are rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected name filing may be appealed by written administrative review to the Registrar under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) within 30 days of refusal, with opportunity to demonstrate acquired distinctiveness or amend the distinctive element. Upon a final refusal, the applicant may apply to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta for judicial review. A name search report (NUANS) cannot be extended past 90 days; a new report and filing are required after expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible as the Alberta-registered office provided the address is a physical street address in Alberta (not a post office box) and the virtual-office provider accepts service of process during ordinary business hours. For manufacturing activities under ISIC 3240, a separate commercial operating premises must be maintained if production occurs in Alberta. Use of a virtual office alone does not demonstrate commercial substance for tax-treaty or CRA purposes.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (fixed fee for low-risk standard entity)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c. B-9 ('ABCA'), ss. 13-18 (incorporation, certificate of incorporation, registered office, and first directors); Unlimited Liability Corporation provisions introduced by the Business Corporations Amendment Act, 2018 (proclaimed in force); Business Names Registration Act, RSA 2000, c. B-8; Corporate Registry fee schedule under Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, Government of Alberta; filings accepted online through the Corporate Registry (CORES) portal or by paper at Corporate Registry, 3rd Floor, 10155 102 Street, Edmonton, Alberta, and through authorized Alberta Registry Agents.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 2 under the ABCA) accompanied by Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors, resulting in a Certificate of Incorporation issued under the seal of the Registrar of Corporations.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital or escrow account requirement under the ABCA for an Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation. The sole subscriber may subscribe for one common share at a nominal CAD 0.01 per share fully paid in cash. Escrow is required only where a securities exemption or investor immigration capital guarantee so mandates; for ULC pass-through eligibility, share capital and subscription records must be kept current and supported by board documentation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the subscriber subscribes for one common share of the Corporation at CAD 0.01 per share, fully paid, and the President is authorized to issue the share in the securities register. RESOLVED THAT the registered office is fixed at [Legal Address], [City], Alberta, as filed with the Registrar, and the law firm [Firm] is appointed as registered agent. RESOLVED THAT [Name] is appointed President, [Name] is appointed Secretary, and [Name] is appointed Treasurer, each to serve until the first annual general meeting. RESOLVED THAT the officers are authorized to open bank accounts, complete Etsy and Stripe onboarding, and execute all filings necessary to maintain this Corporation in good standing under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta).

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, through an authorized Alberta Registry Agent or the CORES name search facility.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed corporate name in English and French for search against the Provincial Corporate Registry database. Verify that the name is distinguishable from all existing corporate, trade, and reserved names in Alberta and that the 'ULC' designation is permissible. If the preferred name is not available, reserve a first and second alternate name to ensure statutory distinctiveness before filing the Articles of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and two alternate names
Name Search Report issued by an authorized Registry Agent
Name Reservation Request (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name report identifies a conflict or confusing similarity, select the next available alternate and pay the applicable reservation fee; if the report is factually incorrect, submit a written request to the Registrar for re-review with the conflicting record holder's consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator and, where engaged, a licensed Alberta corporate law advisor; documents are prepared for submission to the Registrar of Corporations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Articles of Incorporation in Form 2 containing the Alberta ULC-specific statement that the liability of the shareholders is unlimited, the class structure of common shares without par value, any transfer restriction, the registered office address, and the name and residential address of at least one founding director. Execute the Articles by the incorporator, complete the Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors, and include the director's signed consent in the formation record.
required_dossiers: Executed Articles of Incorporation (Form 2) with ULC unlimited-liability statement
Notice of Registered Office
Notice of Directors
Consent of first director(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar returns the package for deficiency, amend the Articles and Notices and re-execute; a corrected package may be refiled without payment of a new search fee if the deficiency is cured before the original filing is certified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing and Payment of Statutory Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction (CORES online portal, or paper filing at the Edmonton Corporate Registry).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into CORES using the verified account of the law firm or authorized Registry Agent, upload the executed Articles and Notices, pay the CAD 400 incorporation fee using corporate credit, debit, or agent account, and obtain the CORES transaction number. For paper filing, include the fee with the physical submission; all enclosed documents must be properly signed and dated.
required_dossiers: Executed Articles of Incorporation and related Notices
Valid Name Reservation or Name Search Report
Payment of CAD 400 incorporation fee
Signed authorization from the incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected on validation checks, correct the data entry or document deficiency and resubmit the same transaction without an additional registration fee within 30 days; if rejection is due to payment failure, contact the Corporate Registry help desk to confirm the payment and re-submit the filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Registry Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar certifies the Articles of Incorporation and issues the Certificate of Incorporation. Record the Alberta corporate access number and verify that the ULC designation appears on the registry system. Order a certified Registry Extract to evidence legal existence, registered office, and directors for banking, Etsy, and Stripe onboarding.
required_dossiers: CORES filing receipt
Certified copy of Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of Incorporation
Registry Extract request
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains a name, office address, or director typographical error, apply for formal correction of the certificate by filing a Notice of Correction with supporting evidence; processing is completed within two to five business days free of charge for Registrar errors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Canada Revenue Agency Business Number Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Business Registration Online (BRO) portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the newly incorporated ULC with the CRA for a Business Number and, if applicable, GST/HST and payroll accounts. Confirm the legal name, Alberta registered office, first director particulars, and start date. Obtain the CRA Business Number letter and include it in the corporate governance file for bank account opening and e-commerce payment applicant verification.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Alberta registered office address and contact details
Director and officer identification records
CRA Business Registration Online application reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA flags duplicate business number records or identity verification fails, call the CRA Business Window (1-800-959-5525) and provide the incorporation number and certified Registry Extract; resubmit the BRO application with corrected officer details.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance and Initial Annual Return
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry (CORES) and the Corporation's board of directors.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting, adopt the unanimous shareholder agreement if desired, open the corporate minute book, issue share certificates, and maintain the securities register and register of directors and officers. File the initial Annual Return with the Corporate Registry within 60 days of incorporation, and thereafter file the Annual Return before each anniversary date in the Company's own annual return cycle to remain in good standing.
required_dossiers: Corporate minute book with share certificates
Register of directors, officers, and shareholders
Initial Annual Return submitted through CORES
Registered office and contact information confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Annual Return is rejected for missing information, amend and refile through CORES immediately; if late-filing penalty is assessed, submit a written request to the Registrar for penalty cancellation citing the corrected filing date and good-faith cure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Development and Business Licensing Department of the operating municipality (e.g., City of Calgary License Centres or City of Edmonton Business Licensing) in conjunction with Alberta Safety Codes Authority and Alberta Labour and Immigration, Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) program.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Trade and Business Licence for Light Manufacturing (Miscellaneous Products) and Development Permit for Manufacturing Use, issued under Alberta's Municipal Government Act, RSA 2000, c. M-26 and applicable municipal business licensing bylaw.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA), Environmental Assessment and Approvals Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categorical exclusion / registration-tier activity. Die-struck brass enamel badge manufacturing is a small-scale light industrial process; a mandatory Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) is not triggered. AEP registration or approval is only required if process wastewater is discharged to ground or stormwater sewer, or if waste streams exceed the de minimis quantities in Alberta's Waste Control Regulation (AR 192/1996).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process discharge to groundwater or stormwater; wastewater limited to neutralized sanitary sewer flows meeting municipal sewer bylaw limits (pH 6.0-9.5, suspended solids under municipal threshold). VOC and particulate emissions from powder preparation and kiln firing must be controlled with local exhaust filtration and kept below Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives, with hazardous acidic rinse waste manifested and hauled by a licensed waste carrier under the Hazardous Waste Regulation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety and Building Code certificates of compliance issued by the local Safety Codes Officer under Alberta's Safety Codes Act; structural load inspection for kiln, polishing benches, and storage racks; Alberta OHS workplace clearance for the production floor, including WHMIS/GHS SDS management, emergency response plan, and, where preferred, a Certificate of Recognition (COR) under the Partners in Injury Reduction program.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); online portals: Business Registration Online (BRO) and My Business Account (MBA) via canada.ca
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For an Alberta ULC, foreign investors must first complete provincial incorporation through Alberta Corporate Registry (Alberta Registries) to obtain the certificate of incorporation and corporate access number. The corporation must then apply to the CRA for a Business Number (BN) by filing Form RC1, 'Request for a Business Number', or by using the CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) portal, selecting the corporate income tax account (RT) and GST/HST account (RT). The applicant must submit the certificate of incorporation, articles, registered office address in Alberta, and non-resident shareholder information if applicable. A non-resident representative must attach a signed Form RC59 authorization. The CRA issues a nine-digit BN followed by a two-letter program code and four-digit reference number (e.g., 123456789 RT0001), which constitutes the statutory tax identification number for all federal and Alberta provincial tax accounts administered by the CRA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a domestic check-the-box election; an Alberta ULC is a taxable Canadian corporation and must file a T2 corporate income tax return on an entity-level basis for CRA purposes. However, an Alberta ULC is eligible for pass-through classification for U.S. federal tax purposes under Treasury Regulation § 301.7701-3 by filing IRS Form 8832, allowing it to be treated as a disregarded entity or partnership by its U.S. shareholders. Canadian hybrid mismatch rules under the Income Tax Act apply where such classification creates a deduction/non-inclusion mismatch, and may deny deductions or require inclusion adjustments. No other statutory entity-level classification election is available under the Income Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of total gross worldwide taxable supplies in a single calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters; a person exceeding this small-supplier threshold must register for GST/HST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not impose a mandatory real-time electronic fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime for invoices. GST/HST registrants must issue tax invoices containing prescribed information under section 221 of the Excise Tax Act and retain records in Canada for six years. Returns and remittances must be filed electronically where annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 50,000. E-invoicing is voluntary and may be exchanged via PEPPOL-compatible systems; there is no CRA pre-clearance or API validation before issuance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A GST/HST registrant may zero-rate exports of tangible personal property, such as hard enamel lapel pins, where the goods are exported as part of the supply and the registrant retains documentary proof of export. Supplies of goods are zero-rated if the registrant ships or delivers the goods to a destination outside Canada, including by common carrier or freight forwarder. Services supplied to a non-resident person are generally zero-rated unless the service relates to real property situated in Canada or tangible personal property situated in Canada; services performed wholly outside Canada are zero-rated. Input tax credits attributable to zero-rated exports are fully refundable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A) filed with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill or other transport document showing exported goods
Freight forwarder's certificate or carrier's proof-of-export document
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank records evidencing receipt of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits will claw back zero-rated treatment and input tax credits if a registrant cannot produce adequate proof of export within the required period. The normal reassessment period is four years from the date of the return, extended to ten years where misrepresentation or fraud is shown. False statements or gross negligence in claiming export zero-rating attract a penalty under section 285.1 of the Excise Tax Act of 25% of the amount assessed, plus arrears interest. Wilful tax evasion may result in prosecution under section 327 of the Excise Tax Act with fines of up to CAD 250,000 and imprisonment for up to two years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a free convertibility regime for both current and capital account transactions. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are permitted without prior approval or surrender obligations, subject solely to standard corporate filings, tax compliance, and FINTRAC anti-money laundering reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or forced conversion of export proceeds is required. Receipts may be converted at prevailing market rates. Exporters must maintain supporting documentation for audit and comply with FINTRAC reporting thresholds where applicable.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for cross-border digital EMIs including Stripe and PayPal for merchant acquiring and payouts. No Canadian EMI license is required for standard e-commerce operations provided full AML/KYC compliance and beneficial ownership verification are maintained.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote corporate onboarding is fully permitted. Directors may complete KYC through secure video verification or power of attorney; physical appearance is not mandated for standard Alberta ULC entities absent specific risk indicators.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta corporate registry extract, director identification documents, and signed beneficial ownership declaration
Corporate resolutions, bank statements, and evidence of legitimate business activity for die-struck enamel pin manufacturing

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections via SWIFT MT103 or domestic wires using purpose codes such as 'Capital Contribution' or 'Equity Injection'. All transactions require corporate resolutions and must satisfy FINTRAC verification requirements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements cleared through SWIFT MT103 or issuance of Commercial Letters of Credit. Trade disbursements must be supported by commercial invoices, shipping documents, and purchase orders.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (AR) under Business Corporations Act (Alberta), s. 217
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after each fiscal year-end; if no fiscal year-end is filed, within two months after the incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the ULC to non-compliance status and a monetary penalty for every completed year of default; persistent failure (typically two consecutive years) results in administrative dissolution after notice by the Registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including Alberta Corporate Tax return schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal year-end, regardless of residency
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equals 5% of the balance owing plus 1% per full month of delay for up to 12 months; repeated failure may also trigger criminal prosecution under the Income Tax Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Register update and ongoing record maintenance (Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book) certified by the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Maintained at corporate registered office (available for inspection by members and properly served legal process)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous obligation; updated no later than 15 days after any change to directors, officers, or shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Misfeasance and inability to rely on the proportionate liability shield for the ULC's unlimited shareholders; a court may order rectification and impose costs; failure to produce registers on demand can lead to contempt proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A distributing corporation (offering securities to the public) must always have an independent auditor. A non-distributing ULC (such as the subject hard enamel pin entity) is exempt from the mandatory audit if all shareholders pass an unanimous written resolution providing that no auditor shall be appointed under section 154 of the Business Corporations Act (Alberta).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Alberta ULCs not listed on a public exchange may choose Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS); if the ULC is a reporting public entity, IFRS is mandatory.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta's Annual Return confirms registered office, general director information, and corporate access details. The ULC's internal shareholder register is the authoritative record for ownership; no separate provincial UBO schedule is required for the standard private ULC. Upon any share transfer, the minute book must be updated with share transfer documents, consent resolutions, and an updated Securities Register immediately, and the director filing confirmation should be revised at the next annual return.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – USD 8,000 (if audit is not waived by unanimous shareholder consent)

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
